findings.claim: _show crashed on a cat-file "SPEC missing" header when the path held a space

verdict.text: Both round 1 findings are fixed and the fixes break nothing they touch.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1 to r7 all pass; "stamp green: 30c2986744c5a6573896d2a2d953c70bbf367cf8980c6fecc26d1027040795ed".
A found object's header is "OID TYPE SIZE" and never echoes the spec, so the trailing-word test cannot misread a found object, even for a path that itself ends in " missing".
It commits, deletes and restores "docs/how/my page.md", so the verification-commit walk asks cat-file for the spec at the deletion commit.
Under the old code that header splits into three fields and `int("missing")` raises, so the test fails without the fix.
It asserts exit 0 and an empty due list.
Compared the last lines of .claude/rules/docs-layout.md with apm/claude/.apm/instructions/docs-layout.instructions.md: they match, and both describe commit order.
f1: resolved at src/kmctl/review_due.py:209, which treats headers ending in " missing" or " ambiguous" as no text.
The rule's last line now matches the package copies.
